title: Choose how thick the Pen draws before you draw
goal: With the Pen in hand the tool bar offers a colour and nothing else, so there is no way to say how thick the next line should be until after you have drawn it. Drawing an icon at 2 px means drawing the first stroke at 4, picking it, and thinning it, every single time you start. Every other drawing tool lets you set its weight up front.
notes:
Found while shipping the-pen-keeps-the-thickness-you-last-chose, which made the Pen REMEMBER a weight (AnnotationStyles.penStrokeWidth, read through EditorState.armedPenStrokeWidth). What is missing is a way to SET it without a path to set it on.

The gate is EditorView.showsStrokeWidthRow, which falls back to activeTool.usesStrokeWidth; that is false for .pen because Tool.usesStrokeWidth is written as "has an annotationShape that is not highlight" and a path is not an AnnotationShape (VectorPath.swift). The store already answers for the Pen: AnnotationStyles.strokeWidth(for: .pen) and setStrokeWidth(_:for: .pen) both route to penStrokeWidth, exactly the way paint(for:)/setPaint(for:) route to penInk. So this is mostly showing the row and wiring its commit to setStrokeWidth(_:for: activeTool), plus deciding what EditorView.editedStrokeWidth reads when a PATH rather than an annotation is picked (selectedAnnotation is nil for a path today).

Watch the icon-frame rule while doing it: IconStrokeWeight.startingWidth only thins a line whose armed width is still the stock 4, so arming the Pen at anything else correctly stops a 24px frame thinning it (IconStrokeWeightTests.anArmedPenIsNotThinned). A row that writes 4 back on open would silently re-enable the thinning.
acceptance: With the Pen in hand and nothing picked, the tool bar offers a thickness alongside the colour swatch
Setting it there and then drawing produces a path at that weight, with the line under your hand already at it
The number shown is the weight the Pen is armed with, and it agrees with what a path drawn a moment ago was set to
A walk sets the weight with the Pen in hand, draws, and claims the number

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) Shortest version: do NOT invent a new bar control. Every other drawing tool's Width lives INSIDE the popover the one toolbar swatch opens (EditorView.strokeWidthSlider in stylePopover); the Pen already wears that same one swatch (Tool.colorControl == .toolColor). So the whole feature is letting that row through for the Pen and routing its commit. A bespoke pen-only width chip on the bar would be a second idiom for one number.

Adversarial review (2): discoverability. With the Pen in hand the swatch's tooltip says 'Path Color', which actively says colour is all that is behind it. Putting a Width row behind a swatch that promises only colour is a row nobody opens. Changing the tip to 'Path Style' (matching 'Text Style' / 'Annotation Style') is part of the work, not a nicety.

Adversarial review (3): the icon-frame rule collides with the number shown. IconStrokeWeight.startingWidth only thins a line whose armed width is still the stock 4, so on a 24px icon frame a Pen that still says 4 draws a 2. The row will therefore read 4 while the path lands at 2, for exactly one value. Choosing any other weight makes them agree again. This ambiguity is not the Pen's: a rectangle's Width row has had it since the icon rule landed, because the model cannot tell 'still stock' from 'deliberately 4'. Out of scope here; recorded in the audit's rough and checked against the queue.

Adversarial review (4): Pen in hand with a path PICKED (press P over a finished path). The Width row will arm the Pen and NOT restyle the picked path. That is deliberate: the Colour row in the same popover already behaves exactly that way (setAnnotationPaint falls through to arming when selectedAnnotationLayer is nil, and a path is not an annotation), and a picked path's weight already has a home in Appearance > Outline > Thickness, which also feeds the Pen back (rememberAnnotationDefaults). Two rows in one popover disagreeing about what they touch would be worse than one rule: this popover is what the NEXT path comes out as.

Shipped in b746d885. Tool.usesStrokeWidth answers yes for .pen (a stroke tool with no AnnotationShape), which lets EditorView's existing Width row through into the popover the Pen's one swatch already opens; setAnnotationStrokeWidth and previewAnnotationRestyle gained a penIsTheOneBeingStyled branch, since styleTargetShape is nil for the Pen and every shape-keyed line was quietly doing nothing. Tooltip 'Path Color' -> 'Path Style'. No new bar control.

Verification, honestly: 7740 tests green, including two new ones that prove the chain the walk would have proven about the numbers (AnnotationStylesTests.thePenHasAWidthToSet, IconStrokeWeightTests.aWidthChosenOnTheBarIsWhatTheNextPathComesOutAt). Acceptance 1-3 are verified at the model layer, NOT on screen, and acceptance 4's walk is written but never ran: the Mac's screen was locked for the whole task, so every walk returns status locked. Requested a sweep naming pen-width-before-you-draw-walk.json and the edited assertion in pen-arms-its-colour-walk.json ('Path Color' -> 'Path Style'); it runs once the screen is unlocked.

Rough that EARNED a task: the row reads 4 on a 24 px icon frame while the line lands at 2, because IconStrokeWeight cannot tell a stock 4 from a typed 4. Reproduced at the model level, filed p2 as the-pen-s-width-row-shows-the-weight-the-line-wi (p2 rather than p1 because it could not be confirmed in the running app). It predates this row and affects every shape tool's Width too.

left rough: the Width sits under the whole colour picker, so it is the last thing in a tallish popover and is one click away rather than readable on the bar. That is what every other drawing tool does and a pen-only width chip would be a second idiom, but for icon work the weight is the setting changed most, so it may want to come out onto the bar. Not filed: it is a UX judgment for the user, and it is in the audit's evaluate and rough where they can react to it.

The Pen's toolbar swatch now opens on a Width beside its colour (tooltip 'Path Style'), and what you set there is what the next path comes out at. Shipped in b746d885, shared code so Next has it. 7740 tests green, two new ones proving the number shown is the number drawn, on an icon frame and off it. NOT verified on screen: the Mac was locked all task, so the walk written for it (pen-width-before-you-draw-walk.json) could not run; a sweep is requested. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-16-pen-width.json
